name: InterSystems Caché
tagline: InterSystems' MUMPS-lineage object/SQL database, superseded by IRIS and winding down maintenance.
description: Caché was InterSystems' database from 1997 to 2018: a MUMPS-descended engine storing data in hierarchical 'globals' with object and SQL projections, plus the Ensemble integration layer. It ran a huge share of hospital systems and some notable science projects. InterSystems replaced it with IRIS in 2018, froze it at the 2018.1 line, and has said no Caché/Ensemble maintenance releases are planned after March 31, 2027 (macOS maintenance already ended in 2024). Support contracts continue, but every remaining installation should be planning its IRIS migration.
statusNote: Superseded by InterSystems IRIS (2018). Frozen at 2018.1.x; InterSystems plans no maintenance releases after March 31, 2027 and recommends migrating to IRIS.

pricing.notes: Existing customers only; new licences go to InterSystems IRIS.

scale.notes: ECP application servers for scale-out reads and mirroring for HA/DR.

strengths: Globals storage gives very fast hierarchical reads and writes
Same data accessible as objects and SQL without mapping layers
Proven at scale in hospital systems for two decades
Migration path to IRIS is vendor-supported and largely in place
weaknesses: End of maintenance releases is announced for March 2027
Proprietary ObjectScript skills are increasingly scarce
useCases: Keeping existing Caché/Ensemble applications supported until migration
Planning in-place conversion to InterSystems IRIS
